title: Etaleness of a morphism between smooth schemes from its relative differential
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:X\to S$ and $q:Y\to S$ be smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $g:X\to Y$ satisfy $qg=p$. Write $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^1_{Y/S}$ for their sheaves of relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and $g^*$ for module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. The universal derivations induce an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $c_g:g^*\Omega^1_{Y/S}\to\Omega^1_{X/S}$, locally given by $a\otimes db\mapsto a\,d(g^\sharp b)$. For every point $x\in X$, the morphism $g$ is etale on some open neighbourhood of $x$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] if and only if the induced map of stalks $(c_g)_x:(g^*\Omega^1_{Y/S})_x\to\Omega^1_{X/S,x}$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules. No field, Noetherian, separatedness, or constant-relative-dimension assumption on $S,X,Y$ is imposed.

source.place: BLR 2.2 Corollary 10, printed p.41 (PDF p.48), equivalence (a) and (b); primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED. proof.text: Apply the pointwise clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-cotangent-etale-criterion] to the same schemes $S,X,Y$, with structural maps $p,q$ and $h=g$. The equation $qg=p$ is exactly its requirement that $h$ be an $S$-morphism. Its map $dh$ is $c_g$: both send $a\otimes db$ to $a\,d(g^\sharp b)$ by their displayed universal-derivation formula. Thus its assertion for the given $x$ is exactly that $g$ is etale on an open neighbourhood of $x$ if and only if $(c_g)_x$ is an isomorphism. Its pointwise clause assumes only smoothness over $S$; the equal-rank hypothesis occurs solely in its additional determinant clause and is not used here.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q127-8b55bf6e7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the report and the full statement of lem-sfb-smooth-cotangent-etale-criterion. The item is exactly the cited node's pointwise clause: S, X, Y arbitrary schemes, X→S and Y→S smooth, h an S-morphism, and 'h is etale near x iff (dh)_x is an isomorphism'. Setting h=g works because qg=p. The maps c_g and dh are the same map (adjoint to b↦d(g^♯b), using the same differentials and pullback nodes). The cited node's equal-rank hypothesis applies only to its determinant clause. The cited node is in the same unit (sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability), is present on the base, has empty proof_deps and does not cite the item, so there is no cycle. Brief §2 says a special case of an existing node is handled by citing it, so this is not D1/D2. There are no new nodes, and the base item had no proof steps to lose. All six stmt_deps exist and none is merged; def-pc-module-stalk-functor covers (c_g)_x. The statement is true: the forward direction follows from the first fundamental sequence plus Ω_{X/Y}=0; the converse follows from unramifiedness plus the fibrewise flatness criterion and Stacks 02GU (morphisms.tex l.8318), conditions (1)⇔(4). I tested id, étale-over-S schemes, Frobenius on A¹_{F_p}, a point into A¹, X=∅ and a non-reduced S. Duplicate grep found only specializations (lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials, lem-sfb-smooth-tangent-isomorphism-etale) and the cited more general node; the overlap could be merged later. BLR is WANTED (not local) and no SGA is cited. The Mathlib searches cover all three kinds and 'no match' is credible. No fixes and no tool_uses.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_morphism_cotangent_isomorphism_etale {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ S) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : g ≫ q = p) [Smooth p] [Smooth q] (x : X) : (∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Etale (U.ι ≫ g)) ↔ IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map (q.relativeDifferentialsPullbackMap g ≫ (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsCongr (g ≫ q) h).hom))
